---
title: "Grouped Linear CUDA Executor"
format: html
---

`cellerator::modeling::cuda::GroupedLinear` applies one linear transform per
expert to an expert-major ragged batch. Each expert owns a row-major weight
matrix `W[e]` with shape `[output_features, input_features]`. A monotonic host
offset array assigns rows to experts; repeated offsets represent empty experts.
The activation and result buffers are contiguous row-major arrays whose first
dimension is the total number of routed rows.

The executor calls cuBLAS once for each nonempty segment. It does not evaluate
inactive experts, gather rows, allocate scratch storage, or synchronize. This
simple implementation establishes the mathematical and buffer contract; it
does not claim the launch efficiency of a fused grouped-GEMM implementation.

## Forward and reverse mode

For each expert segment, forward computes

```text
Y[e] = X[e] W[e]^T
```

Reverse mode computes `dX[e] = dY[e] W[e]` and `dW[e] = dY[e]^T X[e]`.
Each output gradient has an explicit `GradientMode`: overwrite uses beta zero,
and accumulate uses beta one. Empty activation segments need no forward or
input-gradient work. An empty expert's weight gradient is zeroed in overwrite
mode and left unchanged in accumulate mode.

FP16 input, weights, output, and gradient buffers use FP32 accumulation through
cuBLAS. Tensor Op math is enabled for the executor's owned handle, while cuBLAS
selects whether a given shape uses Tensor Cores. FP32 buffers use FP32 math.

## Ownership and execution

The executor borrows its expert weight views and retains their addresses and
extents; the caller must keep the underlying parameter allocations alive and
unchanged while operations use them. Activations and result buffers are also
borrowed. Operations accept an explicit `Stream` and return after enqueueing
work. Separate executors can submit concurrently to independent streams. A
single executor is not safe for simultaneous host-thread calls because its
cuBLAS handle is rebound to each supplied stream.

The host row offsets and per-expert weight views are validated when the
executor is constructed. Feature dimensions and expert segment lengths must fit
cuBLAS's integer dimensions. No model lifecycle, expert identity, routing
policy, placement, or parameter ownership is prescribed here.

## Validation boundary

The device smoke fixture checks a ragged three-expert layout (including an
empty expert), forward products, and gradient products. Focused V100 numerical
results for FP16 storage with FP32 accumulation and FP32 execution are in the
[validation report](../planning/v100-framework-2026-10-29/REPORT.md). These
cases are correctness evidence, not a performance comparison against cuBLAS.
